prompt.context: Our client, Dark Sky, is a small manufacturer of unmanned (i.e. remotely piloted) data collection aircraft. Dark Sky produces the Assessor, an aircraft originally designed for unmanned weather exploration. In 2006, the United States military began purchasing Assessors for use in Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) missions. The Assessor is profitable, but sales have stagnated and the client wishes to grow.
prompt.question: What are some steps Dark Sky could take to achieve growth?

clarifying_info.a: Dark Sky's only customer is the U.S. Military.

Dark Sky has a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee contract with the U.S. Military for Assessor sales. The contract has been extended in the past and is up for renegotiation; the Military has agreed to a marginal fee (price) increase to account for inflation.

clarifying_info.q: Does Dark Sky have capacity to expand?
clarifying_info.a: The firm has additional capacity and is positioned to strengthen any division of the workforce if required, e.g. sales force, manufacturing, R&D.

clarifying_info.q: What is special about the Assessor aircraft?
clarifying_info.a: Dark Sky designs a unique aircraft that is launched from a catapult device; the aircraft can be launched from ships at sea or from harsh terrain such as desert or mountains.

clarifying_info.q: Does Dark Sky sell other products?
clarifying_info.a: Dark Sky only sells the Assessor, but has designed prototypes specifically for military operations.

There are approximately 20 competitors that manufacture unmanned aircraft. Though too small to purchase a competitor, Dark Sky has been considered an acquisition target. Dark Sky's lack of growth in recent years concerns potential buyers.

exhibits.title: Revenue ($, Million)
exhibits.shows: A bar or line chart showing Dark Sky's annual revenue in millions of dollars from 2004 to 2014.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Revenue in $ millions (0–5); X-axis: years 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2014; revenue appears to start very low around 2006 and grows to approximately $5 million by 2010–2014.

exhibits.title: New Product Sales Forecast, 2015 — New Product Sales (# of aircrafts)
exhibits.shows: A table showing three new aircraft prototypes (SeaBird, SandBird, JointBird) with forecasted unit sales to the Navy and Army respectively, and the price per aircraft for each model.
exhibits.data: SeaBird: Navy 50, Army --, Price $220,000; SandBird: Navy --, Army 60, Price $210,000; JointBird: Navy 38, Army 52, Price $180,000

exhibits.title: Impact of New Product on Assessor Sales
exhibits.shows: A table showing the cannibalization effect each new aircraft would have on existing Assessor unit sales.
exhibits.data: SeaBird: cannibalization 40%; SandBird: cannibalization 70%; JointBird: cannibalization 90%

framework: Organic growth — internal levers: increase military penetration (negotiate more Assessor sales), product development (new aircraft models, training services, accessories/add-ons), new market entry (international markets, Border Patrol, police, news channels), diversification (new product for new market), pricing adjustment (Assessor price increase)

Inorganic growth — external levers: joint venture with a firm to increase market access or develop beyond Dark Sky's current capability, merger/acquisition (or position as acquisition target given stagnant growth)
Opportunity assessment — evaluate which new aircraft prototype maximizes revenue given Assessor cannibalization

questions.prompt: Exhibit 1a: How many units were sold in 2014?
questions.guidance: Read revenue from the chart (~$5 million) and divide by the known price of $100,000 per unit to get unit count.

questions.prompt: Exhibit 1b: What was the revenue growth rate from 2006 to 2010?
questions.guidance: Read 2006 revenue (~$500k) and 2010 revenue (~$5,000k) from the chart, then apply percentage growth formula.

questions.prompt: Exhibit 2: To maximize short-term growth, which new aircraft should Dark Sky introduce?
questions.guidance: For each scenario, calculate (1) remaining Assessor revenue after cannibalization at the new price of $110,000/unit, (2) new product revenue from Exhibit 2 unit sales, and (3) total revenue. Compare across all four scenarios (Assessor only, +SeaBird, +SandBird, +JointBird). Note: price increase to $110k has been agreed; baseline is 50 Assessor units with no new launch.

math.setup: Assessor price (post-increase) = $110,000/unit; Baseline Assessor units = 50; Cannibalization rates: SeaBird 40%, SandBird 70%, JointBird 90%
steps: With SeaBird: Assessor units = 50 x (1-40%) = 30; Assessor rev = 30 x $110,000 = $3,300,000; SeaBird rev = 50 x $220,000 = $11,000,000; Total = $14,300,000
With SandBird: Assessor units = 50 x (1-70%) = 15; Assessor rev = 15 x $110,000 = $1,650,000; SandBird rev = 60 x $210,000 = $12,600,000; Total = $14,250,000
With JointBird: Assessor units = 50 x (1-90%) = 5; Assessor rev = 5 x $110,000 = $550,000; JointBird rev = (38+52) x $180,000 = 90 x $180,000 = $16,200,000; Total = $16,750,000
math.answer: JointBird yields the highest total revenue at $16,750,000

brainstorming.prompt: What are some steps Dark Sky could take to achieve organic and inorganic growth?

categories.name: Organic — Market Penetration
ideas: Negotiate additional Assessor unit sales to the military
Lobby for expanded ISR mission scope to increase demand

categories.name: Organic — Product Development
ideas: Develop new aircraft models tailored to specific military branches (SeaBird, SandBird, JointBird)
Offer training services for drone operators
Develop aircraft accessories or add-ons (sensors, payloads)

categories.name: Organic — New Market Entry
ideas: Sell the Assessor in international allied-nation military markets
Domestic non-military: Border Patrol, police departments, news channels, research institutions

categories.name: Organic — Diversification
ideas: Develop a product (e.g. ground-based sensor system) for a market outside defense
Expand into commercial UAV market (agriculture, surveying)

categories.name: Organic — Pricing
ideas: Negotiate a larger price increase beyond the agreed inflation adjustment
Introduce tiered pricing based on mission capability

categories.name: Inorganic — Partnerships
ideas: Joint venture with a larger defense contractor to gain market access
Partner with a technology firm to develop next-generation payloads

categories.name: Inorganic — M&A
ideas: Acquire a small competitor to add capacity or complementary product
Position Dark Sky as an attractive acquisition target to capitalize on its unique technology

recommendation: Dark Sky should introduce the JointBird to the U.S. Military to maximize short-term revenue growth; projected total 2015 revenue is $16.75M versus $5.5M for the Assessor-only scenario.
Simultaneously pursue medium-term organic growth through new market entry (domestic non-military agencies, allied nations) to reduce single-customer dependence.
risks: Launching JointBird cannibalizes 90% of Assessor unit sales, reducing Assessor revenue to $550,000 — management must assess whether it is profitable to continue producing the Assessor at that volume or reallocate those resources.
Single-customer concentration (100% U.S. Military) creates contract renewal risk; new markets are essential for long-term stability.
Competitive response: 20 competitors exist; a new product launch may trigger pricing pressure or accelerated competitor development.
Payback period on investment in manufacturing a new aircraft type is unknown and must be quantified.
next_steps: Quantify profitability (not just revenue) for each aircraft under the Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee structure to confirm JointBird is the best margin option.
Assess manufacturing timeline: can Dark Sky begin producing a second new model (e.g. SeaBird) in the following year after JointBird launch to further grow revenue?
Evaluate whether Assessor production at 5 units/year is economically viable or if those resources should be redirected.
Analyze international and domestic non-military market entry feasibility (regulatory approvals, export controls, sales force requirements).
Explore partnership or acquisition opportunities to accelerate growth and strengthen Dark Sky's profile as an acquisition target.
